findings.highlight: It was a choice I made with fatal conviction
findings.evidenceJa: 致命的なまでに、この答えは決まっていた
findings.governingReading: 答えは決まっていた locates the settled answer from the earlier embrace; his inability to act has only now made him realize it.
findings.explanation: An answer already fatally fixed becomes a conscious choice made with fatal conviction.

findings.highlight: A "hero" who will kill many people tonight
findings.evidenceJa: 多くの人間を見殺しにした正義の味方
findings.governingReading: 見殺し identifies failure to save in his self-accusation.
findings.explanation: Leaving people to die becomes killing them directly.

findings.highlight: A powerless human who saves others only for his own satisfaction.
findings.evidenceJa: 私情だけで誰かを助ける無力な人間
findings.governingReading: 私情 contrasts with Kiritsugu discarding personal feelings; it does not specify gratification as the motive.
findings.explanation: Saving from personal feelings becomes saving only for his satisfaction.

findings.highlight: hammer my stopped self in the chest.
findings.evidenceJa: 立ち止まる自分の胸を打つ
findings.governingReading: 立ち止まる自分 means the present self hesitating/standing at the decision.
findings.explanation: The self standing still becomes a stopped self.

findings.highlight: Will I betray myself, who lived through the burning ruins, crying while everyone else died around me?
findings.evidenceJa: 死んでいった人々の声を
findings.governingReading: He asks whether he will betray both the dying people's voices and his former self struggling to survive alone.
findings.explanation: The Japanese names the victims' voices as something he could betray. The English asks only about betraying himself, although the following page still states his obligation to the dead.

findings.highlight: leaving everything I've believed in, everyone who's helped me.
findings.evidenceJa: 今まで信じ、支えてきたモノをなくして
findings.governingReading: 信じ、支えてきたモノ concerns what he has believed and supported, in the abandonment of his own prior self.
findings.explanation: Things he believed and upheld become everyone who helped him.

findings.highlight: Just as I try to leave the room...
findings.evidenceJa: ナイフを戻そうとした瞬間
findings.governingReading: ナイフを戻そうとした瞬間 locates her speech at the attempted safe return of the blade, before departure.
findings.explanation: Her interruption while he withdraws the raised knife becomes while he leaves the room.

findings.highlight: That I won't save them, so it makes sense that they won't save me, either.
findings.evidenceJa: 他人を助けてあげないんだから、他人に助けてもらえないのは当たり前
findings.governingReading: After nobody helped her, the people who fail to help others naturally cannot expect help themselves: her rationalization of their deaths.
findings.explanation: Others refusing help becomes Sakura refusing to save others.

findings.highlight: they're all going to die anyway.
findings.evidenceJa: みんなが殺されるのは仕方ない
findings.governingReading: 殺されるのは仕方ない is her rationalizing their being killed in retaliation for withholding help.
findings.explanation: Their killings being unavoidable/unsurprising becomes everyone inevitably dying anyway.

findings.highlight: I accept her body as hard as I can
findings.evidenceJa: ありったけの力で、桜の体を受け止める
findings.governingReading: 受け止める in this bodily sequence means holding/receiving her into the embrace with all his strength.
findings.explanation: An intensely held embrace becomes accepting her body as hard as he can.

findings.highlight: I've always regretted the fact that I couldn't protect you before.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜を守れなかった今までのことを、ずっと後悔する
findings.governingReading: ずっと後悔する promises enduring regret for past failure, contrasted with regretting the coming commitment.
findings.explanation: Continuing regret becomes always having regretted.

findings.governingReading: 嗚咽 denotes sobbing/choked weeping in her relief and embrace.
肩にかかる specifies their contact/draping across his shoulders within the mutual embrace.
findings.explanation: Her arms reaching his shoulders become merely raised arms.

findings.highlight: All we can do is forgive each other, over and over.
findings.evidenceJa: 今はそう繰り返すしか、互いを許す術がなかった
findings.governingReading: そう繰り返す refers to the just-spoken promise to protect; this repetition is their present means of forgiving each other.
findings.explanation: Repeating his promise as the only way to forgive becomes repeated forgiveness itself.
